title: 2026-11-04_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_830
description: Security monitoring has detected unusual network activity originating from several IoT devices within your network. Initial analysis suggests the presence of the Remaiten botnet malware, which targets routers and other IoT devices. Your task is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malicious activities, and implement appropriate containment measures.
outcomes: Enumerate running and inactive services to identify suspicious activities.
Investigate systemd service activation and scheduling to identify persistence mechanisms.
Correlate network connections and service behavior to identify unauthorized communication.
Apply targeted firewall controls to contain the threat.
Terminate malicious processes and disable persistence mechanisms.
Remove malicious artifacts while preserving forensic evidence.

levels.title: Identify the Beacon Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server.
levels.solution:
1. List all services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
2. Identify suspicious services:
Look for services with unusual names or descriptions. Pay attention to services that are not part of the standard system services.
3. Check the status of suspicious services:
```bash
systemctl status <service_name>
```
4. Identify the service responsible for beaconing:
Look for services that have network-related descriptions or are configured to run periodically.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions that indicate network activity.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl status <service_name>` to check the status and configuration of suspicious services.

levels.title: Determine the Communication Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Identify the suspicious service:
Use the service name identified in TRAINING_LEVEL 1.
2. Inspect the service configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat <service_name>
```
3. Look for the ExecStart directive:
This directive specifies the path of the script launched by the service.
4. Inspect the script to find the communication port:
```bash
cat /usr/local/lib/.botcache/beacon.sh
```
Look for the `c2_port` variable or similar indicators.

hints.content: Look for the ExecStart directive in the service configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Inspect the script specified in the ExecStart directive to find the communication port.

levels.title: Identify the Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigators suspect that the C2 beacon service automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```
2. Identify the timer associated with the suspicious service:
Look for timers with names related to the service identified in TRAINING_LEVEL 1.
3. Inspect the timer configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat <timer_name>
```
4. Verify the timer's schedule and associated service:
Look for the `OnCalendar` directive and the `Unit` directive that specifies the associated service.
